Analysis of transmon qubit layout and electromagnetics
Conceptual Hamiltonian and complexity in quantum chip design
Risk, cost, time, and resource considerations in quantum hardware development

2020-mit-tech-review-emerging-technology.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses quantum jumps and their control in quantum computing.
2020-mit-tech-review-emerging-technology.summary: The talk explores the nature of quantum jumps, challenging traditional views and introducing methods to predict and mitigate errors for more reliable quantum technologies.
key_points: Challenges traditional views of quantum jumps as discrete and random.
Introduces methods to predict and control quantum jumps for error correction.
Explores the implications for more reliable quantum technologies.

2020-pyepr-meeting-energy-participation-.short_description: The talk covers the energy participation ratio (EPR) approach for analyzing superconducting qubits and its implementation in the pyEPR framework.
2020-pyepr-meeting-energy-participation-.summary: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses the EPR method to analyze non-linear elements in superconducting circuits, presenting it as a unified framework for quantum device design and validation.
key_points: Introduces the EPR method for analyzing superconducting qubits.
Describes its application in quantum device design and validation.
Presents the pyEPR framework as a tool for practical implementation.

2019-energy-participation-ratio-epr-for-.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses the energy-participation approach to designing superconducting quantum circuits.
2019-energy-participation-ratio-epr-for-.summary: The talk covers a unified framework for analyzing and designing superconducting qubits using the energy-participation ratio (EPR) method, which is applicable to various non-linear devices and architectures.
key_points: Introduces the energy-participation approach for designing superconducting quantum circuits.
Explains how to calculate the energy stored in non-linear elements using EPR.
Demonstrates practical applications and limitations of the EPR method.
Highlights the unified framework's applicability across different architectures.

2019-quantum-sensing-keynote-padua-italy.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses quantum sensing techniques and superconducting qubits for high-precision measurements.
2019-quantum-sensing-keynote-padua-italy.summary: The talk covers quantum sensing principles, superconducting qubit hardware, and advanced measurement techniques like EPR circuit quantization and real-time control for improving detection efficiency and error correction in quantum computing.
key_points: Improves quantum detection efficiency and error correction in superconducting qubits.
Uses EPR circuit quantization for more accurate measurements.
Focuses on real-time control techniques to enhance measurement precision.
Discusses the application of these techniques in practical quantum sensing scenarios.

2015-2-5d-cqed-coherence-exploring-drawb.short_description: The talk covers the 2.5D multilayer architecture of drawbridge transmon qubits and explores coherence, noise, and quasiparticle dynamics.
2015-2-5d-cqed-coherence-exploring-drawb.summary: This technical talk delves into the design and performance of 2.5D multilayer superconducting qubits, focusing on their architecture, system parameters, coherence enhancement through dynamical decoupling, and quasiparticle behavior.
key_points: Exploration of the 2.5D multilayer architecture for drawbridge transmon qubits.
Discussion on coherence enhancement through dynamical decoupling techniques.
Analysis of quasiparticle dynamics and their impact on qubit performance.

2014-2-5d-circuit-quantum-electrodynamic.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses superconducting qubits and whispering gallery mode resonators for quantum computing.
2014-2-5d-circuit-quantum-electrodynamic.summary: The talk covers design strategies for superconducting qubits using whispering gallery mode resonators, focusing on coherence, coupling, and practical implementation details.
key_points: Designs for superconducting qubits using whispering gallery mode resonators.
Achieving high coherence and strong coupling in 2.5D architectures.
Fabrication techniques like e-beam lithography and bridge-free junction fabrication.
Exploring the 'Energy BBQ' framework to understand Hamiltonian interactions.

2013-superconducting-whispering-gallery-.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses superconducting whispering gallery mode resonators for scalable quantum computing.
2013-superconducting-whispering-gallery-.summary: The talk covers design and properties of superconducting resonators, their integration into qubit architectures, and future research directions in cQED.
key_points: Design and properties of superconducting whispering gallery mode resonators.
Integration of resonators into wafer-scalable qubit architectures.
Future research directions in cQED with multi-qubit systems.

2012-superconducting-whispering-gallery-.short_description: Dr. Minev discusses a wafer-scalable Circuit QED architecture using whispering gallery modes in parallel plate ring resonators.
2012-superconducting-whispering-gallery-.summary: The talk covers the design and optimization of superconducting thin film rings for high-Q whispering gallery modes, focusing on frequency separation, mode degeneracy, and alignment tolerances to achieve scalable quantum computing architectures.
key_points: - Optimized whispering gallery modes for high-Q in parallel plate ring resonators.
- Achieved frequency separation and mode degeneracy lifting.
- Demonstrated alignment tolerances and their impact on Q.
- Discussed challenges in scaling the architecture.

2012-wafer-assembled-whispering-gallery-.short_description: Dr. Minev discusses whispering gallery mode resonators for superconducting qubit architectures.
2012-wafer-assembled-whispering-gallery-.summary: The talk covers the design and simulation of high-Q whispering gallery mode resonators to improve superconducting qubits' performance, focusing on fabrication techniques and quality factor optimization.
key_points: High-Q whispering gallery mode resonators for superconducting qubits.
Fabrication techniques and quality factor optimization.
Simulation results indicating achievable internal Q factors.
Comparison of simulation with experimental data.

2012-whispering-gallery-modes-minev.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses a wafer-scalable Circuit-QED architecture for superconducting qubits and characterizes their properties.
2012-whispering-gallery-modes-minev.summary: The talk covers the design and experimental setup of a wafer-scalable Circuit-QED architecture, focusing on the characterization of superconducting devices at the single photon level, including quality factors, coherence times, and dissipation budgets.
key_points: Introduces a wafer-scalable Circuit-QED architecture for superconducting qubits.
Discusses the design and experimental setup of the architecture.
Characterizes quality factors, coherence times, and dissipation budgets of superconducting devices.
Highlights the importance of single photon level characterization in cryogenic materials.

2011-josephson-junction-arrays-parasitic.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses fluxonium junction arrays and techniques to minimize parasitic capacitance.
2011-josephson-junction-arrays-parasitic.summary: The talk covers the design and optimization of fluxonium junction arrays for superconducting qubits, focusing on reducing parasitic capacitance through theoretical studies and simulations.
key_points: - Minimizing parasitic capacitance in fluxonium junction arrays.
- Using Dolan bridge geometry to reduce ground capacitance.
- Simulating and optimizing junction array designs for superconducting qubits.

2011-josephson-parametric-amplifier-opti.short_description: The talk covers high-fidelity microwave readout using Josephson parametric amplifiers and their simulation for superconducting qubits.
2011-josephson-parametric-amplifier-opti.summary: This technical talk focuses on developing high-fidelity microwave readout techniques for superconducting quantum bits through the use of Josephson parametric amplifiers, detailing simulations to optimize performance parameters like bandwidth and dynamic range.
key_points: Developed a numerical solver for parametric amplifier performance simulation.
Achieved noise-free simulations matching theoretical predictions.
Observed gain suppression and SNR asymmetry in noisy conditions.
Optimized bandwidth by varying quality factor (Q).

t11-7-pictorial-digital-quantum-circuits.short_description: The talk covers digital quantum circuits and their pictorial representations, focusing on symbols, gates, and measurement.
t11-7-pictorial-digital-quantum-circuits.summary: This technical talk delves into the symbolic representation of digital quantum circuits, including Pauli gates, controlled-NOT (cNOT) gates, SWAP operations, and measurement principles. Viewers will learn about gate decompositions, circuit identities, and how to manipulate qubits using these techniques.
key_points: Pictorial identities for digital quantum circuits are essential for standardized communication.
Pauli gates and their decompositions play a crucial role in quantum circuit design.
Controlled-NOT (cNOT) and SWAP operations are fundamental building blocks of quantum circuits.
Measurement principles allow for deferred measurement, simplifying circuit design.

t11-9-concentration-inequalities-and-tai.short_description: The talk covers concentration inequalities and tail bounds for random variables.
t11-9-concentration-inequalities-and-tai.summary: This technical talk provides an overview of various probability inequalities such as Markov's, Chebyshev's, Chernoff-Hoeffding, and others, which are essential tools in analyzing the behavior of sums of independent random variables and understanding their distributions.
key_points: Introduction to Markov's, Chebyshev's, and Chernoff-Hoeffding inequalities.
Explanation of their applications in analyzing random variables.
Overview of various probability tools for understanding distributions.

t21-estimating-observables-from-sampled-.short_description: The talk covers estimating observables from sampled bit strings in quantum computing experiments.
t21-estimating-observables-from-sampled-.summary: This technical talk discusses how to estimate observable properties from classical data obtained through quantum computer experiments, focusing on sampling errors and their propagation.
key_points: Estimation of observables from sampled bit strings.
Analysis of sampling error and its propagation.
Use of the Walsh-Hadamard transform in observable estimation.

t22-bound-sum-of-operators-ala-watrous-m.short_description: The talk covers bounding sums of operators in quantum computing using positive semidefinite operators and Schatten norms.
t22-bound-sum-of-operators-ala-watrous-m.summary: This technical talk delves into proving Lemma 3.3 from Watrous (2018) on bounding the sum of operators with complex weights, utilizing Schatten norms and operator factorization techniques.
key_points: Proves Lemma 3.3 from Watrous (2018) on bounding operator sums.
Uses Schatten norms and operator factorization techniques.
Illustrates the application of complex vector weights in quantum operators.

t23-pec-probaiblity-error-cancelation-no.short_description: Dr. Zlatko Minev discusses probabilistic error cancellation techniques for noisy quantum processors.
t23-pec-probaiblity-error-cancelation-no.summary: The talk covers probabilistic error cancellation methods using sparse Pauli-Lindblad models to mitigate errors in quantum circuits, providing insights into the number of random circuit instances needed for effective mitigation.
key_points: Techniques for probabilistic error cancellation in noisy quantum processors.
Use of sparse Pauli-Lindblad models to mitigate errors.
Calculation of the number of random circuit instances required for effective mitigation.
Analysis of sampling overhead and its impact on error bounds.

t25-random-sampling-and-twirling-of-stat.short_description: Investigates if mixed states and random sampling of states are equivalent in quantum state measurements.
t25-random-sampling-and-twirling-of-stat.summary: The talk explores how noise channels affect qubit states and compares mixed-state ensembles to trajectory sampling, showing that while expectation values match, variances differ due to shot noise.
key_points: Mixed states and trajectory sampling yield identical expectation values.
Variances differ due to shot noise in random sampling.
Twirling procedure is used for analysis.
Results are relevant for understanding quantum state measurements.

t26-many-body-physics-exploring-spin-mod.short_description: Introduces spin models in many-body physics and their application in quantum computing.
t26-many-body-physics-exploring-spin-mod.summary: The talk covers the Anderson model and its extension to spin models, focusing on one-particle density matrices (OPDMs) and integrals of motion in toy models. It provides a beginner-friendly approach for understanding complex systems through simplified frameworks.
key_points: Explains the Anderson model and its extension to spin models.
Introduces one-particle density matrices (OPDMs) for understanding complex systems.
Discusses integrals of motion in toy models.
Provides a beginner-friendly approach to many-body physics concepts.

t27-simple-noise-models-and-gate-fidelit.short_description: The talk covers simple noise models in quantum computing, focusing on depolarizing and bit-flip processes.
t27-simple-noise-models-and-gate-fidelit.summary: This technical talk by Dr. Zlatko Minev reviews basic noise models such as depolarizing and bit-flip channels, connecting them to key concepts like gate fidelity and error mitigation techniques.
key_points: Explains depolarizing and bit-flip noise channels in detail.
Connects noise models to gate fidelity concepts.
Discusses probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) and twirled readout error mitigation (T-REX).
